changes.evidence: Nothing returns Killmonger to the U.S. military after he becomes Black Panther (ep 6) and joins the Guardians of the Multiverse (ep 9). In ep 9 he turns on the Guardians to take Ultron's Stones and is trapped with Zola. In ep 18 Kahhori sends him back to his own world, and no group is shown. Marvel Database lists U.S. Navy, Stark Industries and the Guardians all as former affiliations. The last 'U.S. Military' stage has no source.

In What If...? ep 9 Killmonger turns on the Guardians of the Multiverse and attacks them for the Infinity Stones. That is a real departure (he turns on the group), and he joins no other group afterwards.

In What If...? ep 3 Hank Pym is not a S.H.I.E.L.D. member. He is a former agent, out since before the episode, who acts alone as Yellowjacket to avenge Hope's death on a S.H.I.E.L.D. mission. Marvel Database lists S.H.I.E.L.D. only as a former affiliation. No title on file shows him in S.H.I.E.L.D.
No departure happens on screen in What If...? ep 3. His break with S.H.I.E.L.D. is backstory, and he acts alone through the whole episode. Being caught by Fury and Loki is not leaving a group.

owner_calls.question: V1: this record is two characters, Rocket and Groot, filed as one person. A:by-zombie-sorcerers is likewise three people (Rintrah, Sara and the London Master). Should these stay as combined records or be split into one record per person?
owner_calls.evidence: Marvel Zombies ep 3: Thanos kills both Rocket and Groot in Wakanda. Rintrah, Sara and the London Master are three separate sorcerers, and they die separately in ep 4 (Thor kills Sara and the London Master, the horde kills Rintrah).
